data.title: ABB to Buy Germany's Ziehl-Abegg for $2.22 Billion
data.description:
(06:01 GMT) *ABB to Buy Ziehl-Abegg
(06:02 GMT) *ABB to Buy Ziehl-Abegg for $2.22B
(06:02 GMT) *ABB: Deal Expands Offering for HVAC and Industrial Cooling Applications
(06:03 GMT) *ABB: Acquisition Adds Electronically Commutated Fans to Motion Portfolio
(06:04 GMT) *ABB: Intends to Retain Ziehl-Abegg's Headquarters in Kuenzelsau, Germany
(06:04 GMT) *ABB: Germany Will Remain an Important Location for the Business
(06:20 GMT) ABB to Buy Germany's Ziehl-Abegg for $2.22 Billion

By Adria Calatayud

ABB said it agreed to buy Ziehl-Abegg, a German manufacturer of fans, motors and ventilation systems, for $2.22 billion.

The Swiss engineering group said Monday that the deal expands its offering for heating, ventilation and air conditioning as well as industrial-cooling applications.

Ziehl-Abegg is expected to generate about $1.4 billion in revenue in 2026 and its products are used in HVAC, data centers, clean rooms, medical technology and elevator drives, among other uses.

The acquisition aims to add electronically commutated fans to the portfolio of motors and drives of ABB's Motion business, the company said. ABB said Ziehl-Abegg's profitability is expected to be in line with that of its own operations in the area within three years after closing of the transaction, which is anticipated in the second half of 2027 subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions.

ABB said it intends to retain Ziehl-Abegg's headquarters in Kuenzelsau, Germany, and that it will remain committed to the country.

data.title: Trump hosts meme coin dinner as token drops
data.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump, who has earned hundreds of millions of dollars from his $TRUMP meme coin, said at a dinner for the token’s top holders on Sunday that his support for the cryptocurrency was driven by a desire to strengthen the United States’ economic competitiveness.

“I’m doing it for the United States ... If we don’t do it, China’s going to do it,” Trump told attendees at his golf club outside Washington, according to reports. It was the third time Trump had held a gala for the top owners of his meme coin, which once soared as high as $75 ​but has fallen to a record low of under $1.

The gala’s access and perks are divided by tiers for the 185 holders of $TRUMP, the president’s meme coin. The top 29 investors are invited to a VIP reception, and the top four will receive a “TRUMP 18K Gold Watch”, according to the event’s website.

Attendees qualified for the dinner based on their time-weighted holdings of the $TRUMP ⁠coin from September 30 to November 16. Reports say organizers indicated that 185 crypto wallets met the criteria for Sunday's dinner, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just ​130 wallets when the contest concluded on November 16.

The May 2025 event's biggest $TRUMP holder was China-born crypto billionaire Justin Sun, who had $18.5M of the token. This time, there was no Sun at the event signing ​autographs, as per Reuters.

data.title: Maybank Profit Climbs on Stronger Fee Income, Beating Estimates — Update
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

Malayan Banking posted stronger-than-expected net profit in the third quarter, driven by higher core fee income and net fund-based income.

Malaysia's largest lender by market capitalization said Monday that quarterly net profit rose 4.7% from a year earlier to 2.74 billion ringgit, equivalent to $666.2 million. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha had expected 2.71 billion ringgit.

A 7.7% increase in core fees, led by higher wealth-management and investment banking-related income, supported the bottom line, Maybank said. Net fund-based income also grew, rising 2.3% to 5.12 billion ringgit as net interest margin improved five basis points to 2.07%.

However, net interest income--the difference between interest earned on loans and that paid on deposits--slipped 4.3% to 3.13 billion ringgit, and noninterest income fell 3.2% to 2.38 billion ringgit, it said.

Net impairment provisions for the quarter declined 39% to 215.2 million ringgit.

Maybank Chief Executive Khairussaleh Ramli said that while its diversified businesses and regional operations supported performance, the group remains cautious about the outlook amid global economic challenges and geopolitical uncertainty.

Shares of the Malaysian lender have declined nearly 5% this year, pressured by concerns about funding costs and net interest margins as bond yields rise amid a more hawkish Federal Reserve outlook.

The planned expansion of the Kuala Lumpur Composite Index to 50 constituents from 30, aimed at reducing the index's concentration in financial stocks, has also weighed on sentiment toward the bank, an index heavyweight.

Analysts said a potential rate hike by Malaysia's central bank next March could offer Malaysian banks some respite. Banks' net interest margins have been squeezed as U.S. Treasury yields lift domestic bond yields and funding costs and intense deposit competition pushes lenders to offer higher rates.

A 25-basis-point increase in Bank Negara Malaysia's policy rate could improve Maybank's net interest margin by 2.6 basis points, according to estimates by CIMB Securities, which is overweight on the Malaysia banking sector.

That relief would likely be temporary, however. The potential rate increase is a short-term positive catalyst for banks' margins rather than a structural solution to the sector's funding challenges, CIMB Securities analyst Ei Leen Tan said.

data.title: Tech Sell-Off in Asia Eases But AI Jitters Continue — Update
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui and Kimberley Kao

Asian tech stocks weakened, as they were dragged by Wall Street's losses, but markets came off their lows as several governments moved to address the rout in equities amid faltering confidence in the artificial-intelligence trade.

Sentiment in early Asian trade Monday was battered by heavy losses in U.S. stocks Friday. The Nasdaq 100, a basket of the largest U.S. technology companies tracked by several tech-oriented investment and retirement funds, flirted with bear-market territory on Friday, closing at 25028.98, a nearly 20% fall from its record high last month.

"The latest sell-off reflects growing concerns over stretched technology valuations, the scale and financing of AI-related capital expenditure, and uncertainty over the returns on these investments," Commerzbank Research analysts said in a report. "Stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue guidance from a leading U.S. chipmaker in its latest quarterly earnings report failed to reassure investors."

But the futures markets signaled a potential rebound on Monday, with futures tied to the Nasdaq and S&P 500 last 2.8% and 2.1% higher, respectively.

Though sentiment in Asia remains fragile, it improved through the trading day, given that regulators and market operators in China, South Korea and Taiwan rolled out measures to arrest the turmoil sparked by the global rout in AI stocks.

South Korean chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics eased some losses and were last lower by 2.0% and 2.3%, respectively, dragging the Kospi down over 2%.

China's Shanghai Composite Index and the tech-heavy ChiNext Price Index reversed earlier losses to gain 0.2% and 3.6% respectively. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Tech Index last traded 0.3% higher. Taiwan's Taiex jumped 2.2%.

Japan's markets were closed for a public holiday.

In China, the three main stock exchanges said over the weekend that they will cut the minimum requirement for margin financing to 80% from 100% effective Nov. 30.

In Seoul, officials are preparing a market-stabilization fund and vowed to step up scrutiny of trading activity. They will also ease limits on daily share buybacks for three months starting Tuesday.

Spot gold rose 2.2% to over $3,610 a troy ounce, while spot silver was up 2.7% to $42.35 a troy ounce.

Bitcoin was last 0.9% higher at $61,417.17, but the cryptocurrency will likely struggle to return to the $65,000 level anytime soon, said Linh Tran, market analyst at XS.com. Investors had already been pulling money out of bitcoin exchange-traded funds even before concerns about AI stock valuations spread to risk assets, Tran said. The market is also awaiting the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy decision, which has weighed on sentiment over concerns of a steep rate hike, Tran said.

"The [market] risks are no longer just about AI valuations," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo. "Nvidia's regulatory uncertainty, questions around AI spending, a potential Fed policy mistake and vulnerabilities in leveraged financing could all shape the next market move," she said.

In energy markets, oil futures swung between losses and gains as investors weigh the outlook for global supply conditions.

Shipments of oil through major Middle Eastern chokepoints rose 19% in the third quarter from the prior three months, according to a report published last week by the U.S. Energy Information Administration. The agency said regional crude production reached 23.1 million barrels a day in October, the highest since the conflict began, as producers expand shipments through alternative routes.

"Monthly crude oil flows out of the Middle East have ranged between 80%-90% of pre-war levels in October," said John Oh, an analyst at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, in a report. "Current flows out of the Middle East should see global oil inventories build."

Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures last rose by 0.3% to $83.70 a barrel, while front-month Brent crude oil futures were 0.3% higher at $92.86 a barrel, according to ICE data.

  • Sherry Qin contributed to the report

data.title: Shriram Finance set to join Sensex as Trent exits on December 21
data.description:
Shriram Finance Limited will replace Trent Limited in the benchmark BSE Sensex from December 21, 2026, as part of the latest reconstitution announced by BSE Index Services Private Limited.

In the BSE Sensex 50, Divi’s Laboratories will replace Wipro as part of the same round of changes.

Shares of Shriram Finance responded positively to the announcement. On the BSE, the stock was trading at ₹1,000.45 on November 23, up 2.72 per cent from its previous close of ₹974, touching an intraday high of ₹1,015. The stock’s 52-week range stands between ₹810.20 and ₹1,153.65, with a full market capitalisation of ₹2,35,426 crore.

The Sensex tracks 30 major companies listed on the BSE and is one of India’s main equity benchmarks. Shriram Finance’s share price movements will contribute to the index’s performance from December 21, while Trent’s will cease to do so. The inclusion is expected to raise Shriram Finance’s visibility among investors who track the benchmark.

Funds that replicate the Sensex may need to buy Shriram Finance shares and sell Trent shares. The rebalancing could lift demand for Shriram Finance, while sales by Sensex trackers could put pressure on Trent around the effective date.

Shriram Finance is classified as a non-banking financial company (NBFC) and currently trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of 18.11 on a standalone basis, with a return on equity of 11.38 per cent.
